We need propose retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <=9999 (we can't check price but assume buyable). Need JSON route.

We have target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need break into precursors using templates.

We have template 827966 which gave product: Cc1ccccc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1 (same as target? Actually target has methyl on phenyl ring (para to sulfonamide). The result from apply_template gave same? It gave Cc1ccccc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1 which matches target (maybe same). So template 827966 is a retrosynthetic step? It seems to be a disconnection of sulfonamide? Actually template appears to be a reverse of sulfonamide formation? The retro template likely breaks the sulfonamide bond to give aniline and sulfonyl chloride? Let's see product of apply_template is same as target, meaning template applied to target gave same? Wait apply_template returns precursors. It returned a tuple with one SMILES: 'Cc1ccccc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1' which is identical to target. So maybe template not applicable (no disconnection). So need other templates.

Search for amide break: functional_groups_broken amide gave earlier result list includes reaction_id 1205701 with retro_smarts_template breaking amide to give anilide? Let's inspect that template: retro_smarts_template: '[C:2]-[NH;D2;+0:1]-[c:3]>>O=C(-C-C-c1:c:c:c:c:c:1)-[N;H0;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[c:3]'. This breaks anilide (aryl amide) to give a carboxylic acid derivative? The product side is amide, reactant side is acid plus amine? Actually retro: product (target) is C- NH - aryl. Reactants: O=C(-C-C-phenyl)-N(-C)-aryl. So it splits amide into acid (aryl?) and amine.

Our target has amide: /C(=O)N- attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we can break that amide to give an acid (maybe cinnamic acid derivative) and an aniline.

Thus step 1: break amide to give precursor A: the acid part: maybe Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait acid part is the carbonyl attached to the trans-alkene and phenyl. The amide carbonyl attached to C=C and phenyl. So the acid precursor would be something like: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Actually the acid side is O=C(-C-C-phenyl) where the phenyl is the phenyl of the sulfonamide? Wait the amide carbonyl is attached to the trans-alkene which is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). The amide nitrogen is attached to that phenyl (aniline). So the amide is -C(=O)-N-Ph(N). The amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl with an amino substituent (aniline). So breaking amide yields: acid: O=C(-C=C-Ph) (cinnamic acid) attached to sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the carbonyl carbon is attached to the alkene and sulfonyl phenyl? The carbonyl carbon is attached to the alkene (C=C) and to the sulfonyl phenyl? Wait structure: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl phenyl ring (c2) has a substituent /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph(N). So the carbonyl carbon is attached to the alkene carbon (beta carbon) and to N-Ph(N). So the acid side after breaking amide would be the alkene carbonyl acid: O=C(-C=C-Ph) (cinnamic acid) attached to sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the carbonyl carbon is attached to the alkene carbon (alpha) which is attached to phenyl (c2). So the acid would be something like: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 (cinnamic acid attached to phenyl). The amine side would be aniline with NH2 (c3ccccc3N). So step 1: target -> precursor1 (cinnamic acid phenyl sulfonyl) + aniline.

Let's try to apply template 1205701 to target. Need template_id. The reaction_id 1205701 has template_hash etc. Template ID maybe same as reaction_id? Use template_id as string? Let's try apply_template with template_id "1205701".
